delivery_path.summary: Whether a Delivery of one small Story that reuses the current Operation contracts and changes no architecture plans its scope and its execution in one step with one owner gate, or every Delivery plans them in two steps with two owner gates.

values.tradeoffs: Every Delivery plans its scope in /delivery-plan and its execution in /execution-plan DLV-###, each step with its own owner gate. Today's behaviour and the baseline the light path is measured against: in one measured project, its first Delivery took 78 min from reservation to its first published plan, and its second Delivery's two gates were 6 h apart.

A Delivery the compiler finds eligible, exactly one Story with no software_architect role, no architecture impact, reused current Operation contracts, met dependencies and a size within the owner's story_size_budget limits, plans its scope and its Item topology in one step and one owner gate; approve-scope, reserve-delivery, approve-execution, publish-execution-plan and claim-items then run in order with their checks and refusals unchanged, and every other Delivery takes the standard path. One gate and one planning pass less for a small Story, while reservation and publication run without a pause between them, a Story that needs architecture work can slip through until code review, and with no story_size_budget limit set no Story is eligible.

delivery_path.metric: Per light-path Delivery: time from the proposal's start to the plan's publication, owner gates, model passes on that path, and fallbacks to the standard path with the condition or refused verb that caused each, against the standard path's 2 owner gates and 2 planning passes. Guards: an Item reopened or re-planned because the light path missed architecture or Operation impact, code review conformance findings about path claims, and plan revisions after publication.

promotion.unit: At least 3 light-path Deliveries.
promotion.threshold: A median proposal-to-publication time of at most 30 min with exactly one owner gate per light-path Delivery, and zero reopens or re-plans caused by missed architecture or Operation impact, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

backlog_path.summary: Whether a backlog revision of a small technical or defect Requirement runs the standard epic and root review ceremony, or one reader reviews the story delta and the compiler writes the root review round as a structural check.

values.tradeoffs: Every backlog revision runs the epic review of each changed epic and a root review read by the root reader or panel, whatever the revision's size or kind. Today's behaviour and the baseline the light path is measured against: in one measured project, a technical Requirement whose code was already prepared ran the full ceremony for one small story, and the writer spent most of the time re-reading the flow and its rule set and running the epic and root review steps, although writing the story took a few minutes.

A revision the compiler finds eligible, Requirement mode over an earlier approved revision, a Requirement whose request_kind is technical or defect, and at most the package's max_changed_stories changed or added stories, each technical or defect and all in one epic, is reviewed by one reader of that epic's review round who reads only the story delta, and record-light-root-review writes the root review round from the compiler's structural checks; approval re-checks the eligibility and refuses a light root review the revision has outgrown, and every other revision takes the standard path. One review pass instead of an epic panel and a root reader for a small change, while a cross-story defect between the delta and an unchanged story is caught only by the compiler's structural checks, not by a reader.

backlog_path.metric: Per light-path backlog revision: wall clock from begin-revision to approval, review passes and readers, writer reading time, and fallbacks to the standard path with the reason the compiler reported, against standard revisions of a similar size. Guards: a defect found in Delivery that a root reader would have caught, and backlog revisions reopened after a light approval.

promotion.unit: At least 3 light-path backlog revisions, each replayed as a frozen standard root review. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so revisions replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: A median begin-revision-to-approval wall clock at most 40% of comparable standard revisions, the same verdict and every critical and major finding of the standard replay, and zero revisions reopened for a cross-story defect the light path missed, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

execution_planning.summary: How execution planning writes and reviews the facts an execution plan needs: each Operation contract written and reviewed on its own, or every fact written once in the document that owns it and the revised contracts reviewed together with the Item topology in one pass.

values.tradeoffs: Each Operation contract the plan needs is revised and reviewed on its own through the Operation flow, and a planning definition may be restated in every document that uses it. Today's behaviour and the baseline the bundle is measured against: in one measured project, a Delivery took 342 min from plan start to publication, with two separate contract review loops and 24% of its planning text restated in a contract.

Each execution-planning fact is written once, in the section fact-ownership.json names, and linked from every other document; the revised contracts, the Item records and their Stories and Test Plans take one review layer, read by each revised contract's counterpart. Fewer serial passes and no copies to reconcile, while one bundle is larger than one contract and may lower a single reader's recall, and a revised contract that no Item pins still needs a target commit and refresh-target before publication.

execution_planning.metric: Per Delivery that revises at least one Operation contract or declares architecture impact: execution-planning wall time from plan start to publication; serial model passes on that path; review layers and review-loop minutes; the restated share, the distinct 8-word sequences of any planning document found in another one; and owner rulings recorded once with an id. Guards: valid critical or major findings against the contracts or the topology found after approval, plan revisions caused by contract errors and DELIVERY_OPERATION_UNCARRIED refusals.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries that revise at least one Operation contract or declare architecture impact, run with single_source_bundle.
promotion.threshold: One review layer per plan, at most 5 serial model passes, a restated share under 5%, a median execution-planning wall time at most 60% of the 342 min measured baseline and zero escaped valid critical or major findings, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

implementation_schedule.summary: How the implementation roles of one Delivery Item write: one after another in their approved order, or at the same time in lanes whose approved write scopes are disjoint.

values.tradeoffs: Implementation roles write one after another in their approved order in the Item worktree. Today's behaviour and the baseline lanes are measured against; the slowest path when the plan gives each role its own files.

Implementation roles whose approved lane scopes are disjoint write at the same time in the one Item worktree, ordered only by declared seams, and the coordinator stays the only committer. Shorter implementation wall time, while the plan must declare lane scopes and seams, seam defects surface only at the frozen candidate and token cost per Item rises.

implementation_schedule.metric: Per Item with 2 or more implementation roles besides the Software Architect: implementation wall time from the first implementation role's start to the candidate freeze against the sum of its lane times, mean concurrent writer lanes, lane scope violations found before the coordinator's commit, seam-related critical or major code review findings, QA failures at a seam and environment collisions.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Items with 2 or more implementation roles besides the Software Architect run with parallel_lanes_v1, from at least 2 Deliveries.
promotion.threshold: Implementation wall time at most 70% of the lane-time sum, zero lane scope violations, seam-related critical or major findings per Item no higher than the sequential baseline and zero environment collisions, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

owner_gates.summary: When the owner answers a Delivery's questions: each as soon as it comes up, or in two fixed gates, scope and plan first and review and merge last, with every other question queued in User Decisions until then and never decided by default.

values.tradeoffs: The owner is asked each question as soon as it comes up, and the run waits for the answer even when the work in progress does not depend on it. Today's behaviour and the baseline the gates are measured against: in one measured project, 53% of its first Delivery's calendar hours had nothing running and one weekend stop lasted 41.7 h, and its second Delivery's execution planning waited 61.1 min on questions with no subagent running.

The owner decides the scope, the plan and every Operation or Governance change it needs in gate A, and the Delivery Review and the merge in gate B. Between them a question is queued in User Decisions, only the tasks that depend on it wait, a decision of an at-once class is still asked at once and nothing is decided by default. Fewer stops and less idle waiting, while a queued question holds its dependent tasks until the next gate, a long gate A can overload the owner and the class list can miss a decision the owner wanted asked at once.

owner_gates.metric: Per Delivery: owner stops outside gates A and B; critical-path owner wait, question waits with no subagent running; questions queued and their time from queueing to answer; minutes dependent tasks waited; early gates forced because every remaining task depended on pending questions; idle hours that began with an open question; and status questions from the owner. Guard: every User Decisions row is answered before the work that depends on it runs.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with two_fixed_gates.
promotion.threshold: At most 1 stop outside the two gates per Delivery, and only for an at-once class, a critical-path owner wait outside the gates of at most 15 min per Delivery and zero dependent tasks run before their question was answered, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_panels.summary: How backlog epic and root, Solution Design, Design System, Operation contract and execution-plan bundle reviews read the reviewed documents.

values.tradeoffs: One fresh reviewer per review step reads every lens on its role's own tier. Today's behaviour and the baseline the panel is measured against; the slowest path, since one reader works through every lens in turn.

One fresh read-only reader per lens assignment runs in parallel and replaces the step's reviewer; the read-only reviewer roles run as their -lens variants, on the low tier. The panel changes who reads, never the review loop: switch `review_loop` sets that, so at its `current` the panel keeps the step's own loop and a re-review reruns the whole panel, and at `blocking_delta` a re-review reruns only the assignments that returned a blocking finding. Shorter review wall time, while valid-major recall is still measured against the single reader and a panel major can be overrated.

lens_panel.description: Lens reader variant for review panels.

review_panels.metric: Per review pass on the same document, the panel's valid critical and major findings against the official single-reader review's, and the panel's wall time against the official review's.

promotion.unit: At least 5 panel review passes across at least 2 flows.
promotion.threshold: Panel valid-major recall at least equal to the official review's and panel wall time at most 50% of it, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

mechanical_pass_tier.summary: Which tier runs a backlog, Operation contract or Solution Design writer pass that only applies the fixes a review verdict names, and whether a compiler render, stamp or check step spawns a role at all.

values.tradeoffs: Every writer pass runs on its role's own tier, usually as the resumed writer that still holds the document, and compiler steps run as each flow describes. Today's behaviour and the baseline the -mechanical variants are measured against; a pass that only applies spelled-out fixes still generates every edit at the writer's full tier.

A writer pass whose findings each name their exact fix runs on the owning writer's -mechanical variant, a fresh agent on the low tier, and render, stamp and check steps run as direct entry commands with no role pass. The host contract states per host what a variant changes against its writer's own tier: today a smaller model on one host, and on the other only the fresh context, since its low tier runs the writers' own model and effort; the coordinator starts the variant for every fix pass and the pass record says which ran with its model and effort. The variants' values are placeholders until the frozen-task A/B sets them. Shorter fix passes where the low tier runs a lower model, while the fresh variant re-reads what a resumed writer held and a lower tier may misapply a fix, which the unchanged re-check catches at the cost of a round.

mechanical.description: Writer variant for passes that apply only the fixes a review verdict names.

mechanical_pass_tier.metric: Per mechanical pass, its wall time and output tokens against the base writer's median for the same pass kind, whether the re-check finds the fix incomplete or wrong (rework), and any unrelated edit the re-check finds.

promotion.unit: A frozen-task A/B that sets the tier and host values the -mechanical variants run on, then at least 3 Deliveries run with mechanical.
promotion.threshold: Median apply_findings wall time at most 50% of the base writer's median for the same pass kind, a rework rate no higher than role_tier's over the same period and zero accepted unrelated edits, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_manifest_scope.summary: How far a backlog epic review's input manifest reads beyond the epic: every note reached through the links of the notes it includes, or only the epic's dependency closure, the notes that closure links to or cites and their front-matter relations.

values.tradeoffs: Every note an epic manifest includes expands its own links, so the read set grows with the vault instead of the epic and a small epic is handed about as many paths as a large one. Today's behaviour and the baseline bounded is measured against.

An epic manifest follows links only from the epics, stories and test plans of the epic and its dependency closure, reads each note they link to or cite with that note's front-matter relations one hop further, and expands nothing beyond; the backlog root and the review history are read without their links. A smaller manifest, while evidence behind a linked note's body links or two links out is outside it until the reviewer asks for it, and only the root review, which keeps the transitive read set, reads the whole closure.

review_manifest_scope.metric: Per epic review pass, against the transitive manifest of the same epic and backlog revision: manifest path count, JSON bytes and build seconds; reviewer wall time; valid findings by severity against a transitive shadow review of the same epic and revision, as recall; and each request for evidence outside the manifest.

promotion.unit: At least 5 epic review passes run with bounded across at least 2 backlog revisions, each beside a transitive shadow review of the same epic and revision. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so review passes replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: Valid critical and major recall at least equal to the transitive shadow review's, zero valid critical or major findings found later in the same epic whose evidence lay outside the bounded manifest, and median reviewer wall time at most 70% of the transitive review's, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_loop.summary: How a review loop treats the findings a review returns: which findings start a round, where a minor finding goes, what a re-review reads and whether an independent reader calibrates a critical or major claim before it gates, for backlog, Solution Design, Design System and Operation contract reviews and Delivery code review.

values.tradeoffs: Every review loop runs as today, the baseline the other value is measured against, with a single reader or a lens panel alike: switch `review_panels` changes only who reads, and a panel keeps the step's own loop. Operation and Design System reviews have no minor rule or re-review scope, so a review that approves with only minor findings can still take a fix pass and a recheck, a code review minor stays a note with no owner, and every critical or major claim gates as returned.

Only a critical or major finding starts a round, and only once one fresh calibration reader of the claiming reviewer's role, or for an Operation contract or bundle claim the counterpart of the contract it concerns, on that role's own tier, confirms it. A minor finding becomes a follow-up with an owner role and a revisit trigger, and a re-review reads only the open blocking findings, the changed text and its dependency context. It applies to a single reader and a lens panel alike, and a panel's re-review reruns only the assignments that returned a blocking finding. Shorter review loops, while calibration adds a few minutes whenever a major is real, a wrong downgrade can hide a defect until the shadow judge audits it, and a changed-text re-review can miss a knock-on effect outside the dependency context it is given.

review_loop.metric: Per reviewed document against its matching baseline, a `current` run under the same `review_panels` value: review-loop minutes from review start to final verdict, fixes included; rounds; minor findings fixed in a blocking pass against those recorded as follow-ups; and calibration counts, claimed, confirmed, downgraded and invalid, with calibration minutes.

promotion.unit: At least 5 reviewed documents across at least 2 flows: a contract revision, an epic or root review, a Solution or Design System review, or an Item code review.
promotion.threshold: Median review-loop minutes at most 50% of the matching baseline, zero valid critical or major findings found later in the same document and traced to a skipped minor round or a calibration downgrade, the shadow judge confirming every downgrade, and an owner role and revisit trigger on every follow-up, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_rounds.summary: How many readers and rounds a backlog, Solution Design, Design System or Operation contract review runs, and whether its severities are calibrated: the step's own readers and loop, or one reader, no calibration reader, only a critical finding blocking and at most one re-review of the changed text.

values.tradeoffs: Every review runs the readers switch `review_panels` selects and the loop switch `review_loop` selects, the baseline the other value is measured against.

One reader of the step's reader role, never a lens panel, and no calibration reader, so the reader's severity stands as returned. Only a critical finding starts a writer pass and one re-review, which reads only the open critical findings, the changed text and its dependency context; minor and major findings become follow-ups with an owner role and a revisit trigger, and a critical finding still open after that one re-review goes to the owner's approval gate. A revision's first review reads only its delta. The shortest review loop, while an overrated major is never downgraded and an underrated critical ships as a follow-up, a major that would have changed behavior reaches the approved text, and a delta review can miss a knock-on effect outside the dependency context it is given.

review_rounds.metric: Per reviewed document against its matching baseline, a `current` run under the same `review_loop` value: review minutes from review start to final verdict, fixes included; readers run; rounds; and major findings accepted as follow-ups, with each one's later outcome.

promotion.unit: At least 5 reviewed documents across at least 2 flows: a contract revision, an epic or root review, or a Solution or Design System review.
promotion.threshold: Median review minutes at most 40% of the matching baseline, zero valid critical findings found later in the same document and traced to an accepted major or a skipped round, and an owner role and revisit trigger on every follow-up, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

code_review_panel.summary: Whether Delivery code review reads a frozen candidate with the official code reviewer alone, or also with a lens panel beside it whose calibrated blocking findings join the official result.

values.tradeoffs: One fresh code reviewer reads each frozen candidate through every review pass on its role's own tier and registers the code review result. Today's behaviour and the baseline the panel is measured against: in one measured project, the official reviewer found 8 of the 12 valid majors of one code review pass, and each blocker it misses costs a later repair and re-review round.

One fresh code-reviewer-lens reader per lens assignment reads the same frozen candidate and inputs in parallel with the official code reviewer, which reviews as at single_reader. A panel critical or major finding gates only once a fresh code reviewer on its role's own tier calibrates it and finds that the official result lacks it, and merge-panel registers the one code review result: the official findings and the validated panel findings, each with its source. More blockers caught per pass, as in one measured project, where the panel added 4 valid blockers the official reviewer missed in one pass, while every pass adds the lens readers' tokens and a calibration pass before the merge, and a pass where the panel adds nothing, as that project's next pass did, pays them for no gain.

beside_official.description: Lens reader variant for review panels.

code_review_panel.metric: Per code-review pass: the valid critical and major findings found only by the panel, only by the official reviewer and by both, as the shadow judge rates them; the panel claims calibration confirmed, lowered, ruled invalid and ruled duplicate of another finding; and the wall clock of the combined step, from the freeze to merge-panel, against the official reviewer's alone, from the freeze to its registration, as the panel record of each pass keeps them.

promotion.unit: At least 5 code-review passes run with beside_official across at least 2 Deliveries, the measurement criterion of #347.
promotion.threshold: Union valid critical and major recall above the official reviewer's alone and a combined wall clock at most 120% of the official reviewer's, summed over those passes, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

story_size_budget.summary: Whether backlog planning measures each story against owner-set size limits and proposes a split for a story over them, before its epic review.

values.tradeoffs: Nothing is measured or shown, and the one-review-unit rule stays a reviewer's judgement. Today's behaviour and the baseline the budget is measured against; a story can grow far past one review unit before a Delivery plans it.

The backlog compiler reports each story's measures against the owner's limits, and the Product Owner proposes a split for each story over budget before its epic review; the owner accepts it or keeps the story with a recorded reason. Advisory only: it never fails a check, blocks an approval or rewrites a criterion. More, smaller stories each carry their own planning, review and gate overhead, and a count is only a proxy for one review unit.

parameters.summary: Owner-set limit per story size measure. The package sets no limit: a measure without a limit is reported but never over budget.

story_size_budget.metric: Per backlog revision run with propose_split, stories over budget, split proposals accepted and kept, criteria and scenarios moved with exact coverage, and epic review passes; per story, cycle time from start-item to integration, code review cycles, QA rounds and reopens, compared between stories within and over budget in the same period.

promotion.unit: At least 3 backlog revisions run with propose_split and 3 Deliveries that contain stories planned under it.
promotion.threshold: The owner accepts at least half of the split proposals, stories within budget reach integration with a median cycle time at most half that of stories over budget in the same period, and no split loses, merges or rewords a criterion, creates a dependency cycle or yields a story verifiable only after a sibling lands, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval. A promotion keeps off as the default, since only a value the owner chooses takes parameters, and ships package_limits for propose_split, which a project at that value applies to each limit it leaves unset.

test_cost_budget.summary: Whether backlog planning asks what a Test Plan scenario costs to run, and flags each automation-required scenario that runs more table rows serially than an owner-set limit, so QA plans a split before the epic review.

values.tradeoffs: No planning step asks what a scenario costs to run, so the cost of a long table-driven test shows only in Delivery, after a gate waited for it; the compiler still validates rows and row_split where a scenario states them. Today's behaviour and the baseline the flag is measured against: in one measured project, one test ran 260 rows serially for 58 minutes, 25% of QA's 227-minute final gate, and bounded the implementation's own repair runs too.

backlog_compile.py check --json, the review manifests and delivery_compile.py init list each automation-required scenario whose declared rows exceed the owner's serial_rows limit while its row_split is serial or absent, and QA proposes a split before the epic review: rows sharded into independent groups that can run in parallel or grouped under one shared setup, or the owner keeps the scenario serial with a recorded reason. Advisory only: it never fails a check or blocks an approval. A declared row count can go stale as the table grows and then misses a test, sharding can expose order dependence between rows, and QA fills one more optional field for the flagged scenarios.

parameters.summary: Owner-set limit on the table rows a scenario may run serially. The package sets no limit.

test_cost_budget.metric: Per backlog revision run with flag_serial_rows: the scenarios flagged, split and kept serial with a reason; per Delivery: the wall clock of the longest test in QA's final gate and of the gate itself, compared with Deliveries of stories planned at off.

promotion.unit: At least 3 backlog revisions run with flag_serial_rows and 3 Deliveries that contain stories planned under it.
promotion.threshold: No single test runs longer than a quarter of QA's final gate in those Deliveries, and the gate's median wall clock is at most that of Deliveries planned at off for a similar suite, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval. A promotion keeps off as the default, since only a value the owner chooses takes parameters, and ships package_limits for flag_serial_rows.

test_levels.summary: Whether backlog planning has each automation-required Test Plan scenario declare its level, unit, fixture or live, so QA proves a decision rule in-process and keeps live scenarios for engine or operating-system behaviour, and the backlog reviewer questions every live scenario.

values.tradeoffs: No planning step asks at what level a scenario has to run, so a Test Plan tends to prove every acceptance criterion through its most expensive path, a live scenario, even when the assertion is a pure decision; test_cost_budget does not catch it, since a live table under its limit is never listed and sharding a flagged table keeps every row live, and the compiler still validates level where a scenario states it. Today's behaviour and the baseline the declaration is measured against: in one measured project, a final gate ran 166 live cases in 227 minutes, about 82 seconds per case, and a later story's Test Plan asked for 41 scenarios, most of them live, plus one table scenario with 171 live cluster setups, although about 40 in-process unit tests that ran in about a second already proved the decision rules behind most of them.

Every automation-required scenario states its level, and a fixture or live one also states what has to be real for its assertion to mean something. QA proves a decision rule at unit level over every combination of its inputs, adds one fixture scenario per entry point and decision family, and keeps live for engine or operating-system behaviour; backlog_compile.py check --json and the review manifests list each scenario that states no level or no reason, the test_cost_budget serial-rows list names each flagged scenario's level, and the backlog reviewer asks of every live scenario whether its assertion is a decision. Advisory only: it never fails a check or blocks a review, and only a stated level outside the three values fails check, as at every value. QA states two more optional fields per scenario, a declared level can go stale as the code moves, and a decision proven at unit level rests on the one fixture scenario per entry point to show that the real entry point consults the rule.

test_levels.metric: Per backlog revision run with declared: the scenarios listed without a level or a reason, the live scenarios moved to a cheaper level and the ones kept live with a reason; per Delivery: the live cases and the wall clock of QA's final gate, compared with Deliveries of stories planned at off.

promotion.unit: At least 3 backlog revisions run with declared and 3 Deliveries that contain stories planned under it.
promotion.threshold: The live share of the automated cases in those Deliveries' final gates and the gate's median wall clock are lower than in Deliveries planned at off for a similar suite, no acceptance criterion loses its proving scenario, and no defect found after a passing gate sits in a decision that a unit scenario proved in place of a live one, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

pre_handoff_regression.summary: Whether an Item's candidate goes to Code Review and QA after its implementation's own tests, or only once the automated suites of the earlier stories its change touches, with its own Test Plan targets, pass on that exact candidate.

values.tradeoffs: The implementation proves its own Item's tests and hands the candidate to the readers; the full gate is QA's. Today's behaviour and the baseline the run is measured against: in one measured project, three side effects of a story's change broke 18 cases of an earlier story's suite, QA's first `make test` stopped at its first failure before that group ran, and the readers found them only in round 2, one full reader and repair round of at least 4 h later.

Before the freeze the coordinator runs, under the Item's environment lock and in a private checkout of the exact candidate, the Test Plan automation targets of every earlier story whose integrated Item in a merged Delivery claims a path the change touches, with the Item's own, through the approved diagnostic adapter, or the full approved test command without one, and the freeze refuses until that run passed. A regression in an earlier story's suite is repaired before the readers start, while every freeze waits for that run, a story whose tests exercise code outside its own path claims is not selected, and without a diagnostic adapter the run is the full suite.

pre_handoff_regression.metric: Per Delivery: the blocking findings Code Review and QA raise that are regressions in an earlier story's suite, per review round, and the wall clock of each pre-handoff run.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with touched_suites.
promotion.threshold: Zero blocking findings that are regressions in an earlier story's suite after the first review round of any Item, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

own_target_reuse.summary: Whether QA's final test run on a frozen candidate runs every own Test Plan target of the Item itself, or takes them, but for the ones QA spot-runs, from the pre-handoff regression run that passed on the same tree.

values.tradeoffs: QA's final test run runs every own Test Plan target of the Item itself; at pre_handoff_regression touched_suites it takes only the earlier stories' targets from the accepted run. Today's behaviour and the baseline the reuse is measured against: in one measured project, QA's final test run took 227 minutes, 163 of them on the story's own cases, and about 94% of the run repeated tests the implementation had run on the identical tree in the hours before the handoff.

Where the freeze accepted a pre-handoff run at pre_handoff_regression touched_suites, QA's final test run also takes the Item's own Test Plan targets from it, under the bindings the earlier stories' targets need: the frozen tree, the selection and approved command derived for it, the declared environment of QA's run and the age final evidence may have. QA names at least one own target in a spot-run selection, and the approved test command runs those, every own target that overlaps them and every target the run did not cover. QA's gate stops repeating the new story's cases the run covered, while a flaky own test outside the spot run passes on one green run, QA's coverage audit needs the accepted run's results, so the approved commands must keep each run's JUnit apart, and at pre_handoff_regression off nothing is reused.

own_target_reuse.metric: Per Delivery: the wall clock of QA's final test run, the own targets it reused and spot-ran per Item, and every defect found after a passing QA gate, in a later review round, in the Delivery Review or after merge, in an own target that gate reused.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with spot_run, each with pre_handoff_regression at touched_suites.
promotion.threshold: No defect found after a passing QA gate in an own target that gate reused, and a median wall clock of QA's final test run at most half of the project's final test runs at off for stories of a similar suite, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

qa_gate_order.summary: Whether QA plans and maps every check before it starts its first test command of a round, or starts that command first and plans, maps and drafts its result while the command works.

values.tradeoffs: QA derives its partitions and coverage matrix before it executes anything, then runs its gate and writes its result once the gate has ended. Today's behaviour and the baseline the order is measured against: in one measured project, QA spent 12 to 18 minutes per round writing its result after a gate of several hours, through most of which the model sat idle.

QA starts its first test command of the round in the background, as the host runs a long command, then derives its partitions, maps its coverage matrix and drafts its verification record while the command works, reads the command's output only once the plan and the matrix are written, so the plan-first rule keeps its intent, and waits for it only through `wait --role qa_engineer`. Most of QA's own work overlaps the gate, while any input the command needs, such as a spot-run selection, must be written before it starts, and the mutation, dependency audit and runtime commands still wait for it, since the runner runs one command at a time on an Item.

qa_gate_order.metric: Per QA round: the wall clock from the end of QA's last runner command to the registration of QA's result, compared with plan_first rounds.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with gate_first.
promotion.threshold: A median wall clock from the end of QA's last runner command to the registration of its result at most half of plan_first's, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

epic_review_cadence.summary: When the next backlog epic review starts while the epic reviews run one after another: after the previous review's calibration and the coordinator's record of it, or as soon as the previous review's last reader returns, with calibration and record keeping running beside it.

values.tradeoffs: The coordinator waits for the calibration of one epic review's claims and for its own record of that review before it starts the next epic review. Today's behaviour and the baseline the overlap is measured against: in one measured project, a revision with eight epics and three-lens panels lost 32.7 min over four panel transitions, 3.4 to 4.4 min of each to the severity check and up to 10.9 min to the coordinator, and one transition that overlapped the check took 1.6 min.

The next epic review starts as soon as the previous review's last reader returns; a calibration reader starts for each reader's critical or major claims as soon as that reader returns, and the coordinator records only the fixed claim record at a panel boundary. Shorter gaps between epic reviews on the same frozen inputs, while more agents run at once within the host's limit, a calibration can still be running when the last epic review returns, and every writer action waits for every calibration as well.

epic_review_cadence.metric: Per backlog revision with at least 2 epic reviews run one after another: the time from one epic review's last reader return to the next epic review's first reader start, calibration minutes per claim, and the confirmed critical and major findings against a wait_per_panel run of the same frozen inputs.

promotion.unit: At least 2 backlog revisions run with overlap_calibration, at least 6 epic review transitions in all. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so review transitions replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: A median transition gap under 2 min, and confirmed critical and major findings equal to the wait_per_panel run's on the same frozen inputs, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_scope_record.summary: Whether each backlog epic review records how large its read set is under both review_manifest_scope values, which of its blocking findings cite a note outside the bounded read set, and flags a transitive read set over the owner's budget before its readers start.

values.tradeoffs: Nothing is measured, and an over-large transitive read set shows only when its readers return without real coverage. Today's behaviour and the baseline the record is measured against: in one measured project, a 23-story epic handed each reader 1,002 files and 21.6 MB of sources under transitive, its first panel was discarded, and the switch change and repair cost 64 min before the bounded panel started.

Each epic reader's manifest also derives the other scope's read set and records files, source bytes and manifest bytes for both, flags a transitive read set over the owner's budget so the flow can offer bounded before readers start, and a command reports which blocking findings of the review cite a note outside the bounded read set; the coordinator appends both to a tracked JSON Lines record. The data the review_manifest_scope default is chosen on, while every epic manifest takes a second derivation, about as long as the first.

parameters.summary: Owner-set budget for an epic reader's transitive read set. The package sets no budget: without it no read set is flagged.

review_scope_record.metric: Per epic review: files, source bytes and manifest bytes of both read sets, reader wall time, blocking findings and those citing a note outside the bounded read set, and discarded panels after an over-budget flag was offered or ignored.

promotion.unit: At least 5 epic reviews recorded across at least 2 backlog revisions. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so epic reviews replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: A record for every epic review of those revisions and zero discarded panels after an over-budget flag, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval. The records then decide review_manifest_scope's default, a separate owner decision.

remediation_writers.summary: Who applies the accepted findings of a backlog revision's epic reviews: one Product Owner writer over the union of every epic's review scope, or one writer per epic with findings over that epic's review scope, in parallel, followed by one cross-epic writer that reads only the notes the cross-epic findings name.

values.tradeoffs: One Product Owner writer reads the union of every epic's review scope before its first edit and applies every accepted finding. Today's behaviour and the baseline per-epic writers are measured against: in one measured project, a writer bound to 1,063 inputs, 21.5 MB of sources, read for about 88 min, compacted its context 7 times and had changed no canonical file after 96 min.

After every epic review returns, each epic with accepted findings gets its own Product Owner writer, in parallel within the host's agent limit, whose manifest is that epic's review scope at the review_manifest_scope value in force and whose write scope is that epic's own notes; findings that cross epics go to one cross-epic writer afterwards, whose task binds only the notes those findings name. A writer that only applies named fixes may run as the mechanical variant under mechanical_pass_tier. A shorter read before the first edit and parallel writers, while a fix that a per-epic writer's scope cannot hold must be routed to the cross-epic writer, the parallel writers' edits meet only at the cross-epic pass and the root review, and more agents run at once.

remediation_writers.metric: Per backlog revision: wall clock from the last epic review's return to the last remediation writer's return, input tokens and context compactions per writer, and findings each writer returned for another writer's scope, against a single_writer revision; guard: the root review after remediation finds every accepted finding resolved and no new cross-epic defect.

promotion.unit: At least 2 backlog revisions run with per_epic, each with at least 3 epics with accepted findings. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so revisions replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: Remediation wall clock at most 40% of the single_writer baseline, at most 1 context compaction per writer and zero cross-epic defects the root review traces to a per-epic writer, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

root_review_scope.summary: What a backlog revision's root review reads in full: every story, test plan and the sources they cite, or only the revision's changed stories, their neighbours one dependency edge away and the epics, with every other story as a hash-bound summary in the compiler's whole-backlog graph.

values.tradeoffs: The root reader reads the complete package and every source it cites, whatever the revision changed. Today's behaviour and the baseline the delta read is measured against: in one measured project, a revision that added four stories to 110 ran a three-reader root panel for 98.4 min and about 760 M input tokens, mostly re-reading the sources of unchanged stories, and found three minor record fixes.

The root reader's manifest names in full only the stories this revision changed or added, those one dependency edge away, their test plans, every epic and the review notes, and carries the compiler's graph of every story with its hashes, criteria, scenario count and dependencies, the dependency edges and the root review's compiler facts. A first backlog, a delta over the owner's share of stories and a reader's stated request read the whole package. A root review that scales with the change, while a cross-story defect between two unchanged stories is outside it, and an overlap with an unchanged story shows to the reader only through that story's title and criteria until it asks for the story.

parameters.summary: Owner-set limit on the share of stories a revision's delta may hold for a delta root read. The package sets no limit, so the owner sets it with the value.

root_review_scope.metric: Per backlog revision root review: wall clock, input tokens per reader, manifest paths and bytes, full-read fallbacks with their reasons and reader requests for an unchanged story, and the verdict and findings against a full root review of the same frozen revision; seeded cross-story defects caught.

promotion.unit: At least 3 backlog revisions run with revision_delta, each replayed as a frozen full root review. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so revisions replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: The same verdict and every critical and major finding of the full replay, a median root review wall clock at most 40% of the full replay's, and every seeded cross-story defect reported, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval. A promotion keeps full as the default, since only a value the owner chooses takes parameters, and ships package_limits for revision_delta.

remediation_bookkeeping.summary: Who writes the bookkeeping of a backlog remediation pass: the Product Owner writer copies each recheck's closure rows into the review notes, reruns the expected-hash checks and writes the preservation report itself, or the writer does content fixes only and one compiler command writes the closure rows, the expected manifest hashes and the preservation report from the readers' closure tables and the pinned candidate.

values.tradeoffs: The writer copies closure rows, reruns each expected-hash check and writes the preservation report on its own tier, and a wording change in one record repeats every check. Today's behaviour and the baseline the command is measured against: in one measured project, this tail took about 26 min and 18 min of two writer passes, about 44 min of one backlog revision on the highest tier.

The coordinator writes the readers' closure tables to one JSON file and the writer runs `backlog_compile.py record-rechecks` once after its content fixes: it writes each review note's `Recheck Closures` table, derives the expected manifest hash of every touched scope and writes a preservation report against the pinned candidate, and its `--verify` mode is the writer's check. A tail of minutes instead of a model pass, while the closure tables must already be structured, and the compiler validates the `Recheck Closures` rows of a draft review note only at this value.

remediation_bookkeeping.metric: Per remediation writer pass: the time from the coordinator's fixes-ready message to the writer's final answer, against writer passes of the same kind, and the review notes' closure rows against the readers' closure tables, which must match row for row.

promotion.unit: At least 2 backlog revisions run with compiler, at least 3 remediation writer passes in all. The switch changes only backlog planning, which runs outside any Delivery, so writer passes replace the 3-Delivery default.
promotion.threshold: A median bookkeeping tail of at most 5 min per pass and zero closure rows that differ from the readers' tables, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

reader_waves.summary: How a coordinator starts the independent readers of one review or recheck wave on a host that caps its open agent threads: each as a thread frees up, or all at once after closing every finished worker.

values.tradeoffs: Readers start as the host lets them, and a finished worker or a writer between its passes may keep its thread open. Today's behaviour and the baseline the wave start is measured against: in one measured project, a recheck wave of 12 independent readers ran in batches of at most three for 51 min, where its slowest reader took 20.7 min, and one panel's third reader started about 28 min late behind a finished worker's open thread.

Before a wave starts the coordinator closes every finished worker, the writer between its passes included, counts the free threads and starts every reader of the wave before waiting on any of them; when threads are short it starts the readers with the largest inputs first and says so, and each wave's progress message names its size and its readers running at once. A wave takes about as long as its slowest reader, while a closed writer starts its next pass fresh from its manifest and the findings, without its earlier read history, and a host thread cap below the wave size still batches the rest.

reader_waves.metric: Per review or recheck wave: its wall time against its slowest reader's, its size, the most readers running at once and the minutes between the first and the last reader's start.

promotion.unit: At least 5 review or recheck waves of at least 3 readers each, across at least 2 flows, run with all_at_once.
promotion.threshold: A median ratio of wave wall time to slowest reader of at most 1.2 and readers running at once equal to the wave size wherever the host's thread cap allows it and no rise in writer fix-pass rework, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

calculation_examples.summary: Whether a business rule that computes a number from inputs or configurable parameters must state its formula or a worked input-to-output example in analysis, checked by the analysis challenger and read as the oracle by backlog test plans.

values.tradeoffs: A calculation rule follows the space standard alone, and no review asks how its inputs become the number. Today's behaviour and the baseline the requirement is measured against: in one measured project, a scoring rule whose weights were a tenant setting reached backlog test planning with no computable expected score, and the analysis round trip it caused, a read-only analysis, a direction gate, a source revision with two readers and an approval gate, added about 63 min of agent and owner time while the backlog revision waited.

Every active rule that derives a number carries its formula in its statement or an AC citing it with a worked example, inputs, parameters, expected output and the output after one parameter change; the analysis challenger reports a missing or inconsistent one as a major finding, and a backlog scenario takes its expected value from that formula or example and never invents one. The gap surfaces at analysis review instead of backlog review, while the analyst writes more rows per calculation rule, and the challenger must judge which rules derive a number.

calculation_examples.metric: Per backlog revision: findings that send a calculation gap back to analysis and the minutes from that finding to the approved source revision; per analysis review: calculation example findings raised.

promotion.unit: At least 3 backlog revisions whose sources hold a calculation rule, run with required.
promotion.threshold: Zero findings that send a calculation gap back to analysis from backlog review, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

source_decision_gate.summary: Whether a decision that changes approved analysis documents asks the owner twice, a direction and then the reviewed exact change, or once on the reviewed exact change when its recommended option can be drafted without the owner's input.

values.tradeoffs: The owner picks a direction in a choice gate, the change is drafted and reviewed, and the owner approves its exact content in a second gate, with the run idle between them. Today's behaviour and the baseline the single gate is measured against: in one measured project, one source decision took a 19 min direction gate and then an exact-change gate that stayed open 2 h 10 min although the change was ready with zero findings.

When the recommended option needs no owner input, the change is drafted and independently reviewed before the owner is asked, and one gate shows the options with the reviewed diff and content hash of the recommended one as "approve this exact change"; `approve-package --expected-content-hash` refuses content that differs from what the gate showed, and any other answer falls back to two gates. One owner round trip less when the recommendation is taken, while a draft the owner rejects is drafting and review work spent, and the owner reads a full diff in the first gate.

source_decision_gate.metric: Per source-changing decision: owner gates asked, minutes from the first gate question to the approved write, whether the recommendation was taken, and drafts discarded after a rejected recommendation.

promotion.unit: At least 5 source-changing decisions across at least 2 revisions, run with one_gate_when_drafted.
promotion.threshold: One owner gate for every decision whose recommendation was taken, a median time from the first gate question to the approved write at most half of two_gates', zero approved packages whose content differs from the content hash the gate showed, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

dependent_rebind_gate.summary: Whether the owner gate that approves a change to an approved business-analysis package also shows and approves the mechanical rebinds of the Experience packages it makes stale, or each stale package is found after the approval and gets its own scope gate.

values.tradeoffs: Binding refresh finds an Experience package bound to the previous source receipt after the source approval, and its update opens its own scope gate, even when it only moves the source binding. Today's behaviour and the baseline the combined gate is measured against: in one measured project, such a gate asked nothing new and stayed open 4 h 19 min while nothing ran, the third sequential owner gate of one source decision.

Before the source gate, `experience_compile.py source-impact` lists every approved Experience package that binds the source's current receipt and classes it `mechanical`, when none of its notes cites a changed source row or document, or `semantic`; the source gate opens with one plain sentence of the whole action and approves the mechanical rebinds with the source, and the rebind then runs without a second gate while its scope is exactly those rebinds and `source-impact` still reports a receipt-only change. One owner round less per source change with mechanical dependents, while the owner reads a larger first gate, and a note that depends on a changed rule without citing it is classed mechanical and caught only by the rebind's final review.

dependent_rebind_gate.metric: Per source change that makes an approved Experience package stale: owner gates opened after the source approval for mechanical rebinds, minutes from the source approval to the backlog rebind, and mechanical rebinds whose final review found a source-caused finding.

promotion.unit: At least 3 source changes with at least one mechanical Experience dependent, run with with_source.
promotion.threshold: Zero owner gates opened after a source approval for a mechanical rebind and zero mechanical rebinds whose final review found a source-caused finding, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

rebind_review_scope.summary: What the final snapshot review of an Experience revision that only moved its source receipts reads: the whole package and prototype tree, or the source delta with the package notes once the compiler proves every record and artifact byte unchanged.

values.tradeoffs: Every final snapshot review reads the whole package and its prototype tree at the reviewer's own tier, even for a rebind that changed no record and no prototype byte. Today's behaviour and the baseline the scoped review is measured against: in one measured project, the review of such a rebind took about 28 min and 70.3 M input tokens to confirm the same zero changed bytes the compiler had proved in 2 min, about 72% of the time from the rebind gate's answer to the backlog rebind.

When `experience_compile.py source-impact` reports `source_rebind_only` and no note citing a changed source row or document, the fresh reviewer reads the source diff, the package notes and the attested hashes instead of the prototype tree, reports any claim that depends on the changed source, which starts the full review, and writes the same attestation. A shorter rebind review, while a claim that depends on a changed rule without citing it relies on the reviewer reading the notes, and a prototype screen that shows a changed rule's outcome is not reread.

rebind_review_scope.metric: Per source-only rebind review: its scope, wall time, input tokens and findings, and source-caused findings that a later full review of the same package raised.

promotion.unit: At least 3 source-only rebind reviews run with source_delta, each with a replay of the full review on the same frozen inputs.
promotion.threshold: The same source-caused findings as the full replay, a median review wall time under 8 min and a seeded source change that contradicts a cited claim still producing a finding, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

test_engines.summary: Whether QA's final test run runs the whole suite as one serial command on the Item's one test environment, or runs the partitions the Verification Contract declares in parallel, each in its own private clone on an isolated test engine, and merges them into one piece of evidence.

values.tradeoffs: QA's final test run is one approved command under the Item's environment lock, so the suite runs as one serial job. Today's behaviour and the baseline the partitions are measured against: in one measured project, a local test engine was busy for at least 64% of a Delivery's wall clock, and QA's final gate alone ran 227 minutes for 166 cases.

Where the Verification Contract declares test_partition_command, test_engines and a Test Partitions table and the Environment Contract provisions the engines, run --kind test runs each partition in its own private clone with AGENTROF_TEST_PARTITION and AGENTROF_TEST_ENGINE, longest first, at most one exclusive partition per engine and never more partitions than engines at once, holds the Item's environment lock until the last one ends and merges their results into one record whose exit code is 0 only when every partition passed intact; evidence approval refuses a record that lacks a partition, holds one twice, holds a failed one or runs another command. The gate is bounded by its longest partition instead of the sum, while engines on one host contend for its CPU, memory and disk, a leak between engines gives flaky failures that look like product defects, hidden order dependence between groups surfaces as new failures, and implementation lanes wait for every engine during the gate.

test_engines.metric: Per Delivery: the wall clock of QA's final test run against the sum of its partitions' durations, the host's CPU and memory pressure during the run, and the failures later traced to an isolation leak between engines or to order dependence between groups.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with partitioned.
promotion.threshold: A median wall clock of QA's final test run at most half of the single runs of a similar suite, and no failure traced to an isolation leak between engines that reached a review round, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

test_group_report.summary: Whether a test run counts only its command's exit code and output, or also reads a group report the approved command writes, so that a group that never ran or failed to collect never passes for a green one.

values.tradeoffs: The runner records a test command's exit code, output and identity and knows no groups; whether every group ran is QA's reading of the output. Today's behaviour and the baseline the report is measured against: in one measured project, QA's first gate ran 58 of the suite's 166 cases, since the command stopped at its first failure and two groups never collected, and five of the seven blockers of the next repair sat in tests that first round never ran.

Where the approved Verification Contract declares test_groups and test_group_report, run --kind test, run --kind diagnostic_test and regression-run read the group report the command writes under AGENTROF_VERIFICATION_SCRATCH, record each declared group's status and case counts, and record the run not intact when the report lacks a declared group; evidence approval refuses a final test run whose report lacks a declared group or names one not_collected. A group that never ran or never collected no longer passes for a green one, while the report stays the command's own claim, of which the runner checks only completeness and statuses, and the project's command must write it, which takes a Verification Contract revision.

test_group_report.metric: Per Delivery: the declared groups and test cases each Item's first QA gate run reached against the suite's, the blocking findings a later round raised in tests the first round never ran, and the runs recorded not intact for a missing group.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with refuse_missing_groups, each under a Verification Contract that declares its test groups.
promotion.threshold: Every first QA gate run reaches every declared group, and no later round raises a blocking finding in a group the first round never ran, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

item_qa_tier.summary: Whether each Item's QA gate runs the project's full acceptance command, or the change-level tier for the Item's change while the Delivery runs the integration tier once over the integrated result before its pull request.

values.tradeoffs: Every Item's QA gate runs the full approved acceptance command, whatever the Item's size. Today's behaviour and the baseline the tiers are measured against: in one measured project, one Item's final gate ran 166 live cases in 227 minutes, and a small Item that changes one component pays that same gate.

Where the approved Verification Contract declares a change-level tier and an integration tier, an Item's QA gate runs the change-level tier for that Item's change, and the Delivery runs the integration tier once over the integrated result before its pull request, so the full acceptance command runs once per Delivery instead of once per Item. A small Item's gate shrinks to its own change, while a defect between Items surfaces only at the Delivery's integration run, after the Items are integrated, and a contract without both tiers keeps the full gate per Item.

item_qa_tier.metric: Per Item: the wall clock of QA's final gate and the cases it ran; per Delivery: the wall clock of the integration-tier run and every failure it found that no Item's change-level run had found.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries of 2 or more Items run with change_tier_per_item.
promotion.threshold: A median Item QA gate at most half of the full_per_item gates of a similar suite, and no defect that escaped the integration-tier run, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

item_review_scale.summary: Whether every Item's code review runs the same reader set, or the official reviewer alone reads an Item whose change is under the owner's size limits and the lens panel joins above them.

values.tradeoffs: Every Item's code review runs the reader set switch code_review_panel selects, whatever the change's size. Today's behaviour and the baseline the scaling is measured against.

The coordinator measures the Item's frozen change with the measures the package declares; when every measure with an owner-set limit is at or under its limit, the official code reviewer reads alone, and above any limit the reader set code_review_panel selects reads as today. Smaller Items skip the panel's dispatch and merge, while a small change with a subtle defect loses the panel's second reading, and with no limit set every Item keeps today's reader set.

parameters.summary: Owner-set limit per change size measure. The package sets no limit: a measure without a limit never makes a change small.

item_review_scale.metric: Per Item: its change size measures, the reader set that read it, the code review wall clock, and every valid critical or major finding later found in an Item the official reviewer read alone.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries with at least 5 Items read alone.
promotion.threshold: Code review wall clock of the Items read alone at most 60% of panel-read Items of similar size, and no valid critical or major finding escaping an Item read alone, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

item_cost_report.summary: Whether the Delivery Review reports the Delivery as a whole, or also each Item's fixed cost step by step: code review, QA gate, evidence records, integration and architecture delta.

values.tradeoffs: The Delivery Review carries no per-Item cost table. Today's behaviour; the fixed cost of an Item is reconstructed afterwards from transcripts, if at all.

The coordinator adds a Fixed cost table to the Delivery Review: one row per Item with the wall clock of its architecture delta, implementation, code review rounds, QA rounds, evidence records and integration, each read from the timestamps the Delivery records already hold. The defaults of item_qa_tier and item_review_scale can then be decided on data from several Deliveries, while the review grows by one table and a missing timestamp is reported as missing, never estimated.

item_cost_report.metric: Per Delivery: the share of Item rows with every step measured, and the fixed-cost share of each Item's wall clock.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries run with per_step.
promotion.threshold: Every Item row carries every step it ran, measured rather than estimated, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

requirement_fact_check.summary: Whether a technical Requirement reaches its owner approval question after the compiler check alone, or after one read-only reader also checks its outcome sentences against the contracts, scripts and tests they cite.

values.tradeoffs: Only the compiler checks the Requirement before the owner approves it; the first independent read of its outcomes happens in Backlog Planning. Today's behaviour and the baseline the reader is measured against: in one measured project, the QA and Product Owner passes found four factual errors in one approved technical Requirement, which went back to draft and took a second owner approval.

Before the approval question of a Requirement whose outcomes name contracts, scripts, files or test ids, one read-only reader on the low tier reads those outcome sentences against the files they cite at the current checkout and returns contradictions only; the coordinator fixes each in the draft and recompiles before the owner sees it. One reader step of a few minutes per technical Requirement, while the reader checks only what the outcomes cite, never intent, and a Requirement that cites nothing skips it.

requirement_fact_check.metric: Per technical Requirement: the contradictions the reader found, the Requirement revisions Backlog Planning forced, and the owner gates before the backlog handoff.

promotion.unit: At least 5 technical Requirements across at least 2 backlog revisions.
promotion.threshold: Zero Requirement revisions forced during Backlog Planning with no more than one added reader step per Requirement, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

lane_table.summary: Whether the coordinator tracks parallel lanes in its own context only, or records each lane's start and finish in a lane table under the project-local runtime directory that a restarted session reads before it launches anything.

values.tradeoffs: Lanes live only in the coordinator's context. Today's behaviour; a session restarted after a crash or a context reset can relaunch a lane that had already finished, and a lane's result is found again only by reading its branch or files.

lane_table.py start and finish record each lane's id, role, branch, working directory, state and result note in .agentrof/agent-marketplace/.runtime/lanes/<run>.json, and pending lists the lanes a restarted session still has to launch or resume; start refuses a lane already finished. A restart reads the table instead of guessing, while the coordinator makes two more calls per lane and the table is scratch, never a durable record.

lane_table.metric: Per restarted session: the lanes it relaunched that had already finished, and the minutes from restart to the first lane it launched.

promotion.unit: At least 3 restarted sessions with parallel lanes.
promotion.threshold: No finished lane relaunched after a restart, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

lane_isolation.summary: Whether a delegated fix lane may work in the main checkout, or each parallel fix lane works in its own scratch clone and no delegated lane switches the main checkout's branch.

values.tradeoffs: A delegated lane that fixes a defect on a branch of its own may work in the main checkout. Today's behaviour; two lanes that switch branches there undo each other's working tree, and the coordinator's own branch can change under it.

Each parallel fix lane clones the repository into its own directory under the session scratch and works on its branch there; lane_table.py start refuses a lane whose working directory is the main checkout or inside it, and lane_table.py check refuses when the main checkout's branch differs from the one recorded when the run began. Lanes never collide on one working tree, while each clone costs a fetch and its disk, and a lane must push its branch before its clone is removed.

lane_isolation.metric: Per run with parallel fix lanes: the lanes started, the main checkout branch changes check found, and the clone time per lane.

promotion.unit: At least 3 runs with 2 or more parallel fix lanes.
promotion.threshold: No main checkout branch change and no lost lane work, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_scope.summary: What a role reads in full for a change: the whole package its step names, or the change's impact closure over the vault's typed relations, with every approved, unchanged note outside it as a hash-bound summary, compiler structural checks before any reader starts and a delta-only confirmation re-review.

values.tradeoffs: Every writer and reader reads the complete package its step names, whatever the change touched. Today's behaviour and the baseline the closure read is measured against: in one measured project, a one-story Backlog Planning run spent 31 of its first 68 minutes on readers re-reading approved, unchanged notes, and the confirmation of two small fixes took longer than the fixes.

impact_closure.py derives the changed notes from the approval stamps and their closure over the typed relations and shared contracts; a role reads the closure in full and every approved, unchanged note outside it only as its hash-bound summary, reads beyond it when unsure and records why, and a writer heals a missing relation through impact_closure.py heal and recomputes the closure. The owning compiler's structural check runs before any reader starts, and a confirmation re-review reads only the fixed lines, the notes the fix touches and the open findings. A first approval, a shared contract or policy change and a graph gap widen the read. Reading scales with the change, while a defect between two unchanged notes with no relation between them is outside every reader's closure until a reader suspects it.

review_scope.metric: Per review or writer pass: wall clock and input tokens per reader, closure size against package size, beyond-closure reads with their reasons, relations healed, widenings with their cause and confirmation re-review minutes, and the verdict and findings against a full read of the same frozen inputs; seeded cross-note defects caught.

promotion.unit: At least 5 reviewed changes across at least 3 flows, each replayed as a frozen full read.
promotion.threshold: The same verdict and every critical and major finding of the full replay, a median reader wall clock at most 40% of the replay's, every seeded defect inside a closure reported and every healed relation accepted by its owning compiler, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_fanout.summary: Whether one reader reads every changed unit of a review, or one reader per changed unit reads in parallel and one aggregator decides the cross-unit questions the compilers do not already enforce.

values.tradeoffs: The step's reader, or each lens reader of a panel, reads every changed unit in turn. Today's behaviour; review wall clock grows with the sum of the units.

A review with more than one changed unit, a story, contract, process package, Item or document, spawns one fresh reader per unit in one message, each reading that unit's inputs, and then one aggregator that reads only the readers' findings and the compilers' cross-unit facts and decides overlap, ordering and shared-contract meaning; a single unit keeps one reader. Wall clock bounded by the largest unit, while a cross-unit defect no compiler checks rests on the aggregator, who reads a unit's text only on a stated, recorded request.

review_fanout.metric: Per review with at least two changed units: wall clock against its slowest unit reader, readers run, aggregator requests for unit text with their reasons, and cross-unit findings against a single-reader review of the same frozen inputs.

promotion.unit: At least 5 reviews of at least 2 changed units across at least 2 flows, each replayed as a frozen single-reader review.
promotion.threshold: Every critical and major finding of the replay, a median wall clock at most 50% of the replay's and zero cross-unit defects found later that the aggregator had the facts to report, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_levels.summary: Whether the review levels of a step run one after another, or a level that consumes no earlier level's verdict starts beside it, with approval still waiting for every level.

values.tradeoffs: Each review level starts only after the earlier one is approved, such as the backlog root review after every epic review. Today's behaviour; one full serial wait per review chain.

A level its flow declares independent starts with the earlier level over the same frozen inputs, such as the backlog root review beside the epic reviews once every source is finished, or an Operation contract review beside the execution-plan topology review when neither cites the other's open findings; approval waits for every level, and a blocking fix re-runs every level whose manifest hash it changes. One serial wait less per chain, while a fix found at one level can make the other level's finished read stale and re-run it.

review_levels.metric: Per review chain: wall clock from the first level's start to the last verdict against the levels' summed times, levels re-run because a fix at another level staled them, and findings against a sequential run of the same frozen inputs.

promotion.unit: At least 5 review chains of at least 2 levels across at least 2 flows.
promotion.threshold: Every critical and major finding of a sequential run, a median chain wall clock at most 70% of the summed level times and at most one level re-run per chain on median, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

context_pack.summary: Whether a task starts by reading every flow, skill and reference file its entry binds, or from a derived, hash-bound digest of the rules its role applies at that step, with every source one read away.

values.tradeoffs: A task reads every flow, skill and reference file its manifest binds before it acts. Today's behaviour and the baseline the digest is measured against: in one measured project, a writer spent most of a 33-minute pass reading the full flow and rule set before writing a story of a few minutes' content.

A spawned role receives its pack from context_pack.py build instead of the full required reads: the rules that role applies at that step, required sections, field contracts, refusals and the switch instructions in force, each with the sha256 of its source file. It reads a named source in full only when the pack does not cover its case and records that read and why, and a pack whose source hashes no longer match is refused. Most of the fixed reading time goes, while a rule the digest misses is applied only when the role notices the gap.

context_pack.metric: Per task: minutes and input tokens before the first write or finding, source files read beyond the digest with their reasons, and findings or refusals traced to a rule the digest left out, against tasks of the same entry and role at off.

promotion.unit: At least 10 tasks across at least 3 entries, writers and readers both.
promotion.threshold: A median time to first write or finding at most 50% of the off baseline and zero defects traced to a rule the digest left out, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

step_timing.summary: Whether the coordinator records the start and end of each flow step and role spawn, with its reading, writing, review and waiting phases, in a durable per-run timing record, or records no step timing.

values.tradeoffs: No step or spawn is timed by the package; step_timing.py start and end write nothing. Today's behaviour; where time goes is reconstructed afterwards, if at all.

The coordinator runs step_timing.py start before each step and end after it, records each role spawn with its phase, and ends every run with step_timing.py report --write, a durable per-run record no package command removes. Every step's time and its breakdown are measured as they happen, while each step costs the coordinator two commands and the record grows with every run.

step_timing.metric: Per run: steps and spawns recorded against those run, spans left open, and the report written at the run's end.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries and 3 backlog revisions run with recorded.
promotion.threshold: Every step and spawn of each run recorded with no span left open and a report written for every run, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

step_budgets.summary: Whether each flow step and role spawn is timed against a maximum in minutes and every step that exceeds its maximum is reported at once with its breakdown, or steps run without a budget report. A budget is a maximum, never an expectation: a step may finish well under it, and a budget never blocks, fails or shortens a step.

values.tradeoffs: Steps run without a maximum, and nothing compares a step's time with a budget. Today's behaviour; a slow step shows only when the owner asks.

With switch step_timing at recorded, step_timing.py compares each step and role spawn with its maximum, the package target unless the owner sets one; a step may finish well under it, and only a step that exceeds it is reported, at once, with its reading, writing and waiting breakdown, its largest contributor and the lever that applies, and every run ends with a per-step report against the maximums. Enforcement is reporting only: nothing is blocked, failed or shortened for time. The owner sees every exceeded maximum as it happens, while without step_timing at recorded no time is measured and nothing is reported.

parameters.summary: Maximum minutes per flow step or role spawn; a step may finish well under it. The package ships its initial targets as package limits, since the budgets only report; a parameter the owner sets replaces its target.

step_budgets.metric: Per run: steps over their maximum with their breakdown and named lever, steps with no recorded start or end, and the per-step report's completeness against the steps run.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Deliveries and 3 backlog revisions run with enforced and step_timing at recorded.
promotion.threshold: A per-step report for every run with no step missing, every exceeded maximum reported during the run rather than after it, and no step blocked or shortened for time, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.
